label: lem:dim_osc0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dim_osc0}
Consider $\rho,\theta\in(0,1)$, and $u\colon B_1 \to {\mathbb R}$ a bounded function. If $u$ satisfies the following diminish of oscillation identity for every radius $r \in(0,1]$
\[
\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho r}} u\leq (1-\theta)\operatorname*{osc}_{B_r} u,
\]
then $u$ admits the following Hölder modulus of continuity at the origin
\[
\operatorname*{osc}_{B_r} u \leq Cr^\alpha\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u,
\]
where $\alpha := \ln(1-\theta)/\ln \rho$, $C := (1-\theta)^{-1}$, and $r \in(0,1]$.
head: environment
name: Characterization of Hölder continuity by diminish of oscillation

title: Proof
body_md:
By an inductive argument we have that for any integer $k\geq 0$
\[
\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho^k}} u \leq (1-\theta)^k\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u.
\]
From this identity we can see why $\alpha$ was set to be $\ln(1-\theta)/\ln \rho$. It is the exponent for which we have that $(1-\theta)^k = (\rho^k)^\alpha$, for any $k$.

Let $r\in(0,1]$ and $k=\lfloor \ln r/\ln \rho\rfloor\geq 0$ such that $\rho^{k+1} < r \leq \rho^k$. Then
\[
\operatorname*{osc}_{B_r} u \leq \operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho^{k}}} u \leq (1-\theta)^{k}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u = C\rho^{\alpha(k+1)}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u \leq Cr^\alpha\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u.
\]
This concludes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:holder_weight
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:holder_weight}
Given $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $\mu\in(0,1)$, there exists $C\geq 1$ such that for $u\in C(\Omega)$
\[
C^{-1}[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\Omega)}^{(\alpha)} \leq \sup_{B_\rho(x)\subseteq\Omega} \rho^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu\rho}(x))} \leq C[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\Omega)}^{(\alpha)} .
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $B_r(x_0)\subseteq \Omega$. We will show that for some $C\geq 1$, depending only on $\alpha$ and $\mu$,
    \[
    r^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{r/2}(x_0))} \leq C\sup_{B_\rho(x)\subseteq\Omega} \rho^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu\rho}(x))}.
    \]
    The proof for the lower bound can be obtained in a similar way and is omitted.
    
    For $y\in B_{r/2}(x_0)$ we have $B_{r/2}(y)\subseteq B_{r}(x_0)\subseteq\Omega$ and then
    \[
    r^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu r/2}(y))} = 2^\alpha (r/2)^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu r/2}(y))} \leq 2^\alpha\sup_{B_{\rho}(x)\subseteq\Omega} \rho^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu\rho}(x))}.
    \]

    Let $N := \lfloor 2/\mu\rfloor +1$. Given $y_0,y_1\in B_{r/2}(x_0)$, consider $y_t := (1-t)y_0+ty_1$ so that
    \begin{align*}
    r^\alpha|u(y_0)-u(y_1)|
    &\leq r^\alpha\sum_{i=1}^N |u(y_{(i-1)/N})-u(y_{i/N})|\\
    &\leq \sum_{i=1}^N r^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu r/2}(y_{(i-1/2)/N}))}\\
    &\leq 2^\alpha\sup_{B_{\rho}(x)\subseteq\Omega} \rho^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu\rho}(x))}\sum_{i=1}^N |y_{(i-1)/N}-y_{i/N}|^\alpha\\
    &\leq 2^\alpha N^{1-\alpha}\sup_{B_{\rho}(x)\subseteq\Omega} \rho^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{\mu\rho}(x))}|y_0-y_1|^\alpha.
    \end{align*}
    We conclude after dividing by $|y_0-y_1|^\alpha$ and taking the supremum in $y_0,y_1\in B_{r/2}(x_0)$.
head: environment

label: lem:inter
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:inter}
Given $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $\delta\in(0,1/2)$ there exists $C\geq 1$ such that for $u \in C^1(B_1)$
\[
\|Du\|_{L^\8(B_{1/2})} \leq C\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1}u + \delta^\alpha[Du]_{C^\alpha(B_1)}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given $x_0 \in B_{1/2}$ let
\[
\varphi(x) := \inf_{B_{\delta}(x_0)} u + \delta^{-2}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1}u\1\delta^2-|x-x_0|^2\2.
\]
Let us see that there exists some $y_0 \in \operatorname*{argmin}_{B_{\delta}(x_0)}(u-\varphi)$, see Figure \ref{fig:inter}.

\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{inter.pdf}
\caption{The following construction could be considered a multidimensional version of Rolle's theorem. The paraboloid $\varphi$ satisfies that $\varphi(x_0)\geq u(x_0)$ and $\varphi\leq u$ on $\partial B_{\delta}(x_0)$. Either $\varphi$ touches $u$ at the center $x_0$ or $u$ must cross the graph of $\varphi$ in the interior of the ball $B_{\delta}(x_0)$. Then a downwards translation of $\varphi$ becomes tangent with $u$ at some point $y_0 \in B_{\delta}(x_0)$. At such contact point the gradient of $u$ equals the gradient of $\varphi$, which is bounded by $2\delta^{-1}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u$.}
\label{fig:inter}
\end{figure}  

Notice that $m := \min_{\overline{B_{\delta}(x_0)}}(u-\varphi)\leq 0$ because $\varphi(x_0)\geq u(x_0)$. If $m = 0$ we just take $y_0=x_0$. Otherwise, if $m<0$, then the non-empty set $\operatorname*{argmin}_{\overline{B_{\delta}(x_0)}}(u-\varphi)$ must be disjoint from $\partial B_{\delta}(x_0)$ where $\varphi \leq u$.

By applying the first derivative test at $y_0 \in \operatorname*{argmin}_{B_{\delta}(x_0)}(u-\varphi)$ we obtain that
\[
|Du(x_0)| \leq |Du(y_0)| + |Du(x_0)-Du(y_0)|\leq 2\delta^{-1}\operatorname*{osc}_{\Omega}u + \delta^\alpha  [Du]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{1})}.
\]
The conclusion now follows by taking the supremum over $x_0\in B_{1/2}$.

label: thm:int_hold_est
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:int_hold_est}
    Given $p\in[1,\8]\cap(n/2,\8]$, there exist $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $C\geq 1$ such that for $\Omega\subseteq{\mathbb R}^n$ open, and $u\in C^2(\Omega)$ we have that
    \[
    [u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\Omega)}^{(\alpha)} \leq C\1\operatorname*{osc}_{\Omega}u + \|\Delta u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^{(2-n/p)}\2.
    \]
head: environment
name: Interior Hölder estimate - Laplacian

label: thm:mvf
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Mean value property

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider for $r\in(0,1)$, the average of $u$ over $\partial B_r$. By the change of variable formula
    \[
    \fint_{\partial B_r} u = \fint_{\partial B_1} u(rx)dS(x).
    \]
    Then we compute its derivative with respect to $r$
    \[
    \frac{d}{dr} \fint_{\partial B_r} u = \fint_{\partial B_1} Du(rx)\cdot x dS(x) = \frac{r}{n}\fint_{B_1} \Delta u(rx) dx=\frac{r}{n}\fint_{B_r} \Delta u.
    \]
    The second equality follows by the divergence theorem. Given that $p\geq1$, Hölder's inequality allow us to get
    \[
    \frac{d}{dr} \fint_{\partial B_r} u \leq Cr^{1-n/p}\|(\Delta u)_+\|_{L^p(B_1)}.
    \]

    Notice that the function $r\mapsto r^{1-n/p}$ is integrable in the interval $(0,1)$ if and only if $p>n/2$. By integrating the inequality from $r=0$ to $r=\rho\in(0,1)$
    \[
    \fint_{\partial B_\rho} u \leq u(0) + C\rho^{2-n/p}\|(\Delta u)_+\|_{L^p(B_1)}.
    \]
    We finally recover the desired formula by integrating from $\rho=0$ to $\rho=1$.

\label{cor:wharnack}

label: lem:dim_osc
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dim_osc}
    Given $p\in[1,\8]\cap(n/2,\8]$, there exist $\delta,\theta\in(0,1)$, such that for $u\in C^2(B_1)$ with $\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_1)}\leq \delta$ we have that
    \[
    \operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} u\leq 1 \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad \operatorname*{osc}_{B_{1/3}} u \leq (1-\theta).
    \]
head: environment
name: Diminish of oscillation - Laplacian

title: Proof
body_md: Assume, without loss of generality, that $0\leq u \leq 1$. We now consider two possible alternatives: either $\fint_{B_{1/3}}u$ is $\geq 1/2$ or $\leq 1/2$. In the former case, we get by the weak Harnack inequality that $\inf_{B_{1/3}} u \geq 1/(2C) - \delta$. Otherwise, we apply the same reasoning to $(1-u)$ to conclude that $\sup_{B_{1/3}} u \leq 1-(1/(2C) - \delta)$. In any case, we get the desired diminish of oscillation if we choose $\delta=\theta=1/(4C)$.
head: environment

label: cor:dim_osc
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{cor:dim_osc}
    Given $p\in[1,\8]\cap(n/2,\8]$, there exist $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $C\geq 1$ such that for $u\in C^2(B_1)$
    \[
    \sup_{r\in(0,1)}r^{-\alpha}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_r}u\leq C\1\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1}u+\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_1)}\2.
    \]
head: environment
name: H\"older modulus of continuity - Laplacian

title: Proof
body_md:
Our goal is to show that for some $\rho,\theta \in (0,1)$ we see that $\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho^k}} u \leq (1-\theta)^k$ holds true for any integer $k\geq 0$, so that Lemma \ref{lem:dim_osc0} settles the proof.
    
    Let $\delta,\theta\in(0,1)$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:dim_osc}. Assume that $\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1}u\leq 1$ and $\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_1)} \leq \delta$, otherwise apply the following proof to the function $\bar u:= u/\1\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1}u+\delta^{-1}\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_1)}\2$ that satisfies the required conditions.
    
    Assume by induction that for $\rho:= \min\{1/3,(1-\theta)^{1/(2-n/p)}\}$ and some $k\geq 1$, we have $\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho^k}} u \leq (1-\theta)^k$. The base case $k=1$ is just the conclusion of Lemma \ref{lem:dim_osc}. Then consider $v(x) := (1-\theta)^{-k}u(\rho^kx)$ such that
    \[
    \operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} v =(1-\theta)^{-k}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho^k}} u \leq 1.
    \]
    Using that $\rho \leq (1-\theta)^{1/(2-n/p)}$
    \[
    \|\Delta v\|_{L^p(B_1)} = (1-\theta)^{-k}\rho^{k(2-n/p)}\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_{\rho^k})} \leq \delta.
    \]
    Then by Lemma \ref{lem:dim_osc}, $\operatorname*{osc}_{B_\rho} v \leq \operatorname*{osc}_{B_{1/3}} v \leq (1-\theta)$. Equivalently,
    \[
    \operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho^{k+1}}} u = (1-\theta)^{k}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_\rho} v \leq (1-\theta)^{k+1},
    \]
    which now shows that the geometric decay is valid for every $k\geq 1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $B_{r}(x_0)\subseteq\Omega$, $x,y \in B_{r/6}(x_0)$ distinct, and $\rho=|x-y| \in (0,r/3)$. Notice that $B_{r/6}(x_0) \subseteq B_{r/3}(x) \subseteq B_{r/2}(x_0)\subseteq \Omega$. Consider $v(z) := u((r/3)z+x)$ such that as $z\in B_1$ we have that $(r/3)z+x \in B_{r/3}(x)$.
    
    By applying Lemma \ref{cor:dim_osc} to $v$
    \begin{align*}
    \frac{|u(y) - u(x)|}{|y-x|^\alpha} &\leq \rho^{-\alpha}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{\rho}(x)}u\\
    &= \rho^{-\alpha}\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{3\rho/r}} v\\
    &\leq Cr^{-\alpha} \1\operatorname*{osc}_{B_1} v + \|\Delta v\|_{L^p(B_1)}\2\\
    &= Cr^{-\alpha} \1\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{r/3}(x)} u + r^{2-n/p}\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_{r/3}(x))}\2\\
    &\leq Cr^{-\alpha} \1\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{r/2}(x_0)} u + r^{2-n/p}\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_{r/2}(x_0))}\2.
    \end{align*}
    By taking the supremum over $x,y \in B_{r/6}(x_0)$ and multiplying by $r^\alpha$
    \[
    r^\alpha[u]_{C^{0,\alpha}(B_{r/6}(x_0))} \leq C\1\operatorname*{osc}_{B_{r/2}(x_0)} u + r^{2-n/p}\|\Delta u\|_{L^p(B_{r/2}(x_0))}\2.
    \]
    Finally, we conclude by taking the supremum in $B_r(x_0)$ and using Lemma \ref{lem:holder_weight}.
head: environment
name: Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:int_hold_est}

title: Remark
body_md:
For $\alpha>0$, the function $u(x) := |\ln |x||^{-\alpha}$ over $B_{1/2}\subseteq{\mathbb R}^n$ is not Hölder continuous. We check that, 
    \begin{align*}
    |\Delta u(x)| &= \alpha|(\alpha+1)|\ln|x||^{-(\alpha+2)} - (n-2)|\ln|x||^{-(\alpha+1)}||x|^{-2} \leq  C|\ln |x||^{-(\alpha+1)}|x|^{-2}.
    \end{align*}
    Hence, we have $|\Delta u|\in L^{n/2}(B_{1/2})$ if $\alpha > \min\{2/n-1,0\}$
    \[
    \int_{B_{1/2}} |\Delta u|^{n/2} \leq C\int_0^{1/2} |\ln r|^{-(\alpha+1)n/2}\frac{dr}{r} \leq C\int_{\ln 2}^{\8} \ell^{-(\alpha+1)n/2}d\ell < \8. 
    \]
    This shows that the critical exponent $p=n/2$ cannot be reached in the Hölder estimate.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Notice how the Hölder estimate obtained from $\Delta u \in L^p(B_1)$ with $p\in[1,\8]\cap(n/2,\8]$ is related to the sequential application of Sobolev's embedding and Morrey's embedding. Specifically, the embeddings $W^{2,p}(B_1)\subseteq W^{1,q}(B_1) \subseteq C^{0,\alpha}(B_1)$ hold for $p \in (n/2,n)$, where $q = np/(n-p) > n$, and $\alpha = 1-n/q$. If instead $p\geq n$, we have that $W^{2,p}(B_1)\subseteq C^{0,\alpha}(B_1)$ for any $\alpha \in (0,1)$.
    
    The surprising fact is that, meanwhile the Sobolev/Morrey inequalities require to control each one of the coefficients in the Hessian, the Hölder estimate presented in Theorem \ref{thm:int_hold_est} achieves the same qualitative result with just a control on the Laplacian. This is remarkable given that the Laplacian, being the trace of the Hessian, retains only partial information on the Hessian.

title: Corollary

Given $p\in[1,\8]\cap(n/2,\8]$ and a non-negative integer $k$, there exist $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $C\geq 1$, such that for $\Omega\subseteq{\mathbb R}^n$ open, and $u\in C^{k+2}(\Omega)$ we have that
\[
[D^ku]^{(k+\alpha)}_{C^{0,\alpha}(\Omega)} \leq C\1\operatorname*{osc}_{\Omega}u + \|D^k(\Delta u)\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^{(k+2-n/p)}\2.
\]

label: rmk:lin2
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:lin2}
For a uniformly elliptic operator $F=F(M,x)$, not necessarily differentiable, we can ``linearize'' the equation $F(D^2u,x)=0$ using the Pucci operators instead of the fundamental theorem of calculus. In fact, if we let $f(x) := -F(0,x)$, then any solution of $F(D^2u,x)=0$ satisfies
\[
\mathcal M^-_{\lambda,\Lambda}(D^2u)\leq \underbrace{F(D^2u,x) - F(0,x)}_{=f} \leq \mathcal M^+_{\lambda,\Lambda}(D^2u).
\]
We already pointed out that these inequalities are equivalent to $A:D^2u=f$ for some $A\colon\Omega\to{\mathbb R}^{n\times n}_{\text{sym}}$ such that $\lambda I\leq A\leq \Lambda I$.

head: environment
name: Weak Harnack inequality - uniformly elliptic

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\delta_0,\eta_0\in(0,1)$ and $M_0\geq 1$ be the constants from Corollary \ref{cor:mest} with respect to $\rho := 1/(6\sqrt n)$ and the same ellipticity constants. We will show that Lemma \ref{lem:dimdist} holds for $\delta := \delta_0/(3\sqrt{n})$, $\eta:= \eta_0|B_{1/2}|$, and $M:=M_0$.

Let $Q := \overline{Q_\ell(x_0)}$ be an arbitrary dyadic cube in the decomposition of $\{u>1\}\cap \overline{Q_1}$. Let $r := \ell/(2\rho) = 3\sqrt{n}\ell$, using that $\delta = \delta_0/(3\sqrt{n})$, we see that for the rescalings $v(x) := u(r x+x_0)$ and $g(x):= r^2f(r x+x_0) \geq \mathcal M_{\lambda,\Lambda}^-(D^2v(x))$ we get
\[
\|g\|_{L^n(B_1)} = r\|f\|_{L^n(B_{r}(x_0))} \leq \delta_0.
\]
Given that the predecessor of $Q$ intersects $\{u\leq 1\}$ 
\[
\inf_{B_{1/2}}v = \inf_{B_{3\sqrt{n}\ell/2}(x_0)}u \leq \inf_{Q_{3\ell}(x_0)}u \leq 1.
\]

Now we are in shape to apply Corollary \ref{cor:mest} to $v$ and $g$, obtaining in this way the following estimate for the distribution of $u$ over $Q$
\[
\frac{|\{u\leq M\}\cap Q|}{|Q|} \geq |B_{1/2}|\frac{|\{u\leq M\}\cap B_{\ell/2}(x_0)|}{|B_{\ell/2}(x_0)|}= |B_{1/2}|\frac{|\{v\leq M\}\cap B_{\rho}|}{|B_{\rho}|} \geq |B_{1/2}|\eta_0 = \eta.
\]

By adding this estimate to all the dyadic cubes in the decomposition of $\{u>1\}\cap \overline{Q_1}$
\[
|\{1 < u \leq M\}\cap Q_1| = \sum_Q |\{u\leq M\}\cap Q| \geq \eta \sum_Q |Q| = \eta|\{u>1\}\cap Q_1|,
\]
which concludes the proof.

label: lem:grow_ink
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:grow_ink}
    Let $\rho_0:=1/6$ and $\rho_1:=1/7$. Given $\eta\in (0,1)$ and $F\subseteq E\subseteq {\mathbb R}^n$ closed such that $\overline{B_{\rho_1}} \cap F \neq \emptyset$, and for every ball $B_r(x_0) \subseteq B_1$
    \[
    \overline{B_{r/2}(x_0)} \cap F \neq \emptyset \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad \frac{|E\cap B_{\rho_0 r}(x_0)|}{|B_{\rho_0 r}(x_0)|}\geq \eta,
    \]
    it holds $|(E\setminus F)\cap B_{\rho_1}|\geq 10^{-n}\eta|B_{\rho_1}\setminus F|$.
head: environment
name: Growing ink-spots

title: Proof
body_md:
Given $x_0 \in B_{\rho_1}\setminus F$, let $r = r(x_0) := 2\operatorname*{dist}(x_0,F)$. Consider as well $x_1\in B_{r/2}(x_0) \cap B_{\rho_1}$ such that
    \[
    B_{r/4}(x_1) \subseteq B_{r/2}(x_0) \cap B_{\rho_1} \qquad \text{ and } \qquad B_{r/2}(x_0) \subseteq B_{3r/4}(x_1). 
    \]
    Figure \ref{fig:growing_ink} details the construction of $x_1$.

    \begin{figure}
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{growing_ink.pdf}
    \caption{We may attempt to use Vitali's covering lemma on the set of balls given by $\{B_{\rho_0 r}(x_0) \ | \ x_0 \in B_{\rho_1}\setminus F, r = r(x_0) := 2\operatorname*{dist}(x_0,F)\}$ in order to estimate the measure of $(E\setminus F)\cap B_{\rho_1}$ from below, using the density hypothesis of the lemma. However, we find a problem because $B_{\rho_0r}(x_0)$ may spill outside $B_{\rho_1}$. We fix this issue by considering a new center $x_1$ over the segment from $0$ to $x_0$ with $|x_1-x_0|=r/4$, such that $B_{r/4}(x_1) \subseteq B_{r/2}(x_0) \cap B_{\rho_1}$ and $B_{r/2}(x_0) \subseteq B_{3r/4}(x_1)$. In the exceptional case that $x_0=0$ we take $x_1=0$.}
    \label{fig:growing_ink}
    \end{figure}
    
    Given that $\overline{B_{\rho_1}} \cap F \neq \emptyset$, we get $r\leq 4\rho_1$. Then $B_{3r/2}(x_1)\subseteq B_{7\rho_1}\subseteq B_1$, since $3r/2 + \rho_1 \leq 7\rho_1=1$. Because $B_{r/2}(x_0) \subseteq B_{3r/4}(x_1)$ and $\overline{B_{r/2}(x_0)} \cap F \neq \emptyset$, we also get $\overline{B_{3r/4}(x_1)} \cap F \neq \emptyset$. Then we can apply the hypothesis of the lemma to $B_{3r/2}(x_1)$ and deduce that
    \[
    \frac{|E\cap (B_{r/2}(x_0)\cap B_{\rho_1})|}{|B_{r/2}|}\geq \frac{|E\cap B_{r/4}(x_1)|}{|B_{r/4}|}\frac{|B_{r/4}|}{|B_{r/2}|} \geq 2^{-n}\eta.
    \]
    
    By Vitali's covering lemma, we can extract a countable collection of disjoint balls $\mathcal B \subseteq \{B_{r(x_0)/2}(x_0) \ | \ x_0 \in B_{\rho_1}\setminus F\}$ such that $\sum_{B\in \mathcal B} |B| \geq 5^{-n}|B_{\rho_1}\setminus F|$. Then
    \[
    |(E\setminus F)\cap B_{\rho_1}| = \sum_{B\in \mathcal B} |E\cap (B\cap B_{\rho_1})| \geq 2^{-n}\eta\sum_{B\in \mathcal B}|B| \geq 10^{-n}\eta|B_{\rho_1}\setminus F|,
    \]
    which concludes the proof.

name: Proof of Corollary \ref{cor:mest}

title: Proof
body_md:
Follows as in the proof of Lemma \ref{cor:dim_osc}, assuming first that for $\delta\in(0,1)$ from Lemma \ref{lem:dimdist}, we have $\|f\|_{L^n(B_{3\sqrt n})} \leq \delta$ and $\inf_{Q_3} u \leq 1$. The goal is to show that for every $\mu>0$
\[
|\{u \geq \mu\}\cap Q_1|\leq C\mu^{-\varepsilon}.
\]
Otherwise, we use the homogeneity of the Pucci operator and apply the following reasoning to the renormalized function
\[
\bar u := \frac{u}{\inf_{Q_3}u+\delta^{-1}\|f\|_{L^n(B_{3\sqrt n})}}.
\]

For $M$ and $\eta$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:dimdist}, it follows inductively and once again by the homogeneity of the operator, that for every integer $k\geq 1$,
\[
|\{u>M^k\}\cap Q_1| \leq (1-\eta)^k.
\]
To be precise, the inductive step follows by applying Lemma \ref{lem:dimdist} to $M^{-k}u$. Notice that for $\varepsilon := -\ln(1-\eta)/\ln M$, we can replace $(1-\eta)^{k}$ on the right-hand side with $(M^k)^{-\varepsilon}$.

Given $\mu\geq 1$, let $k$ be a non-negative integer such that $M^k \leq \mu <M^{k+1}$. Then, once we fix $C := M^\varepsilon$, we obtain
\[
|\{u>\mu\}\cap Q_1| \leq |\{u>M^k\}\cap Q_1| \leq (1-\eta)^k = C(M^{k+1})^{-\varepsilon} \leq C\mu^{-\varepsilon}.
\]
If $\mu \in (0,1)$, the desired estimate in the distribution is true because $C\geq 1$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume without loss of generality that $0\leq u\leq 1$ in $B_1$. If
    \[
    \frac{|\{u\geq 1/2\}\cap Q_{1/(3\sqrt n)}|}{|Q_{1/(3\sqrt n)}|} \geq \frac{1}{2},
    \]
    we apply a rescaling of Lemma \ref{lem:wharnack} to get $u\geq \theta := C^{-1/\varepsilon}2^{-(1+2\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}$ in $B_{\rho}\subseteq Q_{1/\sqrt n}$, provided that $\delta := C^{-1/\varepsilon}2^{-(1+2\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}$ and $\rho:=1/(2\sqrt n)$. Otherwise, we apply Lemma \ref{lem:wharnack} to $(1-u)$ to get a similar improvement of the upper bound of $u$.

title: Remark
body_md: Hypothesis $u\in C^3(\Omega)$ can be replaced by $u\in C^2(\Omega)$ in the previous problem. In fact, one can use the translation invariance and the interior Hölder estimate (Lemma \ref{thm:h}) to show that the difference quotient $v_\alpha = (u_{h,e}-u)/h^\alpha \in C^{0,\alpha}_{\text{loc}}(\Omega)$, uniformly in $h>0$. By the interpolation result in \cite[Lemma 5.6]{MR1351007} we recover that $u \in C^{0,2\alpha}_{\text{loc}}(\Omega)$ if $\alpha \leq 1/2$, and otherwise we get $u \in C^{1,2\alpha-1}_{\text{loc}}(\Omega)$. This procedure can be iterated all the way to an interior Hölder estimate for the gradient.

body_md:
\label{lem:abp_deg1}
    Given $[\lambda,\Lambda]\subseteq(0,\8)$ there exist $\delta,\theta,\eta\in(0,1)$ and $M\geq 1$, such that the following holds: Let $\gamma \in [0,1/12]$, $u\in C^1(B_{1})\cap C^2(\{|Du|>\gamma\}\cap B_{1})$ and $f\in L^n(B_1)$ with $\|f\|_{L^n(B_{1})}\leq \delta$, both non-negative functions with
    \[
    \mathcal M^-_{\lambda,\Lambda}(D^2u) \leq f \text{ in } \{|Du|>\gamma\}\cap B_{1}.
    \]
    Then
    \[
        u(0) \leq \theta \qquad \Rightarrow\qquad|\{u\leq M\} \cap B_{1}|\geq \eta.
    \]
head: environment

label: lem:abp_deg2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:abp_deg2}
    Given $[\lambda,\Lambda]\subseteq(0,\8)$ and $\mu\in(0,1/2)$ there exist $\delta,\eta\in(0,1)$, such that the following holds: Let $\gamma \in[0,\mu/2]$, $u\in C^1(B_1)\cap C^2(\{|Du|>\gamma\}\cap B_1)$ with $u\geq \varphi_0^1$, $f\in L^n(B_1)$ non-negative with $\|f\|_{L^n(B_1)}\leq \delta$ such that $\mathcal M^-_{\lambda,\Lambda}(D^2u)\leq f$. Then for $R:=\overline{B_{1-\mu}}\setminus B_{\mu}$
    \[
        A_{\{0\}}^1\cap R \neq \emptyset  \qquad \Rightarrow\qquad|\{u\leq 1\} \cap B_1|\geq \eta.
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x_0 \in A^1_{\{0\}}\cap R$ and consider for $y_0 \in B_{\mu/10}(x_0)$
\[
\varphi_0^1 + (\varphi_{y_0}^1+\mu^2/200) = \varphi_{y_0/2}^2 + c_{y_0}.
\]
For $y_0 \in B_{\mu/10}(x_0)$ we have $\varphi_{y_0}^{1}(x_0) + \mu^2/200>0$ and $\varphi_{y_0}^{1} + \mu^2/200<0$ in ${\mathbb R}^n\setminus B_{\mu/5}(x_0)$. Therefore
\[
\emptyset \neq \operatorname*{argmin}(u-\varphi_{y_0/2}^{2}) \subseteq \{u\leq \mu^2/200\} \cap B_{\mu/5}(x_0)\subseteq B_1.
\]
For every $x_1 \in \operatorname*{argmin}(u-\varphi_{y_0/2}^{2})$ we get that
\begin{align*}
|Du(x_1)| &= 2|x_1-y_0/2|\\
&\geq 2(|x_0-x_0/2|-|x_0-x_1|-|y_0/2-x_0/2|)\\
&\geq 2(|x_0|/2 - \mu/5 -\mu/20)\\
&> \mu/2\\
&\geq \gamma.
\end{align*}
Finally, by the same argument as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:abp}, using the uniform ellipticity at the contact points and the area formula, we conclude that
\[
|\{u\leq 1\}\cap B_1|\geq |A^2_{B_{\mu/20}(x_0/2)}| \geq \eta.
\]

name: Proof of Lemma \ref{lem:abp_deg3}

title: Proof
body_md:
We show instead the result over the domain $B_R$ with $R=3\sqrt{n}$, instead of $B_1$, so we assume $\|f\|_{L^n(B_R)}\leq \delta$. As in Lemma \ref{lem:abp_deg3}, we fix $\mu=1/6$ and $r=1/12$.

    Let
    \[
    m_k(x_0) := \inf_{B_R} (u-\varphi_{x_0}^{2^k}), \qquad R_k(x_0):=\overline{B_{(1-\mu)2^{-k} R}(x_0)}\setminus B_{r2^{-k}R}(x_0), \qquad \theta := (1-\mu)^2 R^2/2.
    \]
    From $u(0)\leq \theta$, we get $m_0(0) \leq \theta$ and $A_{\{0\}}^1\cap \overline{B_{(1-\mu)R}} \neq \emptyset$.
    
    We select a set of dyadic cubes according to the following algorithm: At the $k^{th}$ stage of the algorithm, which starts from $k=0$, we consider a given subset of dyadic cubes from the $k^{th}$ generation of dyadic cubes starting from $Q_1$. One of these cubes, say $Q_{2^{-k}}(x_0)$, is selected if $A_{\{x_0\}}^{2^k}\cap R_k(x_0)\neq \emptyset$. Once a cube is selected, none of its descendants will be considered in the following stages. Otherwise, if the cube is not selected, its immediate descendants will be considered in the next stage.

    By an inductive argument using a rescaling of Lemma \ref{lem:abp_deg3}, we obtain that for every cube $Q_{2^{-k}}(x_0)$ that is considered in the $k^{th}$ iteration we also have that $A_{\{x_0\}}^{2^k}\cap \overline{B_{(1-\mu)2^{-k}R}(x_0)} \neq \emptyset$.
    
    Also by induction and using Lemma \ref{lem:abp_deg3}, we see that if $Q_{2^{-(k+1)}}(x_1)$ is a cube considered in the $(k+1)^{th}$ iteration, descendant of $Q_{2^{-k}}(x_0)$, then
    \[
    m_{k+1}(x_1) \leq m_k(x_0) + 2^{-k}R^2 \leq \theta+2R^2.
    \]
    If $y_0\in Q_1$ is never covered by the selected cubes we find a nested sequence of dyadic cubes $Q_1 \supseteq Q_{1/2}(x_1) \supseteq \ldots$ such that $\bigcap_{k\geq 1}Q_{2^{-k}}(x_k) = \{y_0\}$ and
    \[
    \min\{(u-(\varphi_{x_k}^{2^k}+m_k(x_k)))(x) \ | \ x\in \overline{B_{\mu 2^{-k}R}(x_k)}\} = 0.
    \]
    This implies by the continuity of $u$ that $u(y_0)\leq \theta+2R^2$. If the measure of the set of points not covered is at least $1/2$, the result would now follow for any $\eta\leq 1/2$ and $M\geq \theta+2R^2$.
    
    On the other hand, using Lemma \ref{lem:abp_deg2} we see that if $Q_{2^{-k}}(x_0)$ is one of the selected cubes and now fix $M:=\theta+3R^2$, then
    \[
    |\{u\leq M\} \cap B_{2^{-k}R}(x_0)|\geq \eta_0|B_{2^{-k}R}(x_0)|.
    \]
    Assume that the measure of the union of all the selected cubes is at least 1/2 and let
    \[
    \mathcal B := \{B_{2^{-k}R}(x_0) \ | \ \text{$Q_{2^{-k}}(x_0)$ is one of the cubes selected by the algorithm}\}.
    \]
    By Vitali's covering lemma there exists a disjoint collection of balls $\mathcal B'\subseteq\mathcal B$ so that $\sum_{B\in \mathcal B'} |B| \geq 5^{-n}\left|\bigcup_{B\in \mathcal B}B\right| \geq 5^{-n}/2$. Given that for each $B\in \mathcal B'$ one has $|\{u\leq M\} \cap B|\geq \eta_0|B|$, we obtain that
    \[
    |\{u\leq M\} \cap B_R| \geq \sum_{B\in \mathcal B'} |\{u\leq M\} \cap B| \geq \eta := 5^{-n}\eta_0/2,
    \]
    which conbcludes the proof.
